units.zh: 李崧，深州饒陽人。
units.en: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.
units.literal: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

units.zh: 父舜卿，本州錄事參軍。
units.en: His father Shunqing had been recording officer and military adjutant of that prefecture.
units.literal: His father Shunqing served as recording officer and military adjutant of the prefecture.

units.zh: 崧幼而聰敏，十餘歲為文，家人奇之。
units.en: From childhood Song was quick-witted; by his mid-teens he was already writing essays, and his family marveled at him.
units.literal: Song was clever from childhood; in his teens he could compose essays, and his family regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 弱冠，本府署為參軍。
units.en: At twenty he took a post as military adjutant in the local prefectural office.
units.literal: At the age of twenty he was appointed military adjutant in the prefectural office.

units.zh: 其父嘗謂宗人李鏻曰：「大醜生處，形奇氣異，前途應不居徒勞之地，賴吾兄誨激之。」
units.en: His father once told his kinsman Li Lin, "Where Dachou was born, the boy's looks were odd and his spirit unlike others; he is not meant to waste his life in drudgery—it will be up to my elder brother to teach and urge him on."
units.literal: His father once said to his clansman Li Lin: "Where Dachou was born, his form was strange and his spirit unusual; his future should not lie in vain toil—it depends on my elder brother to instruct and spur him."

units.zh: 大醜即崧之小字也。
units.en: Dachou was Song's childhood name.
units.literal: Dachou was Song's childhood name.

units.zh: 同光初，魏王繼岌為興聖宮使，兼領鎮州節鉞，崧以參軍從事。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang reign, Prince of Wei Jiji served as director of the Xingsheng Palace while also holding the military commission of Zhen Prefecture, and Song went with him as adjutant.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, Prince of Wei Jiji was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the military commission of Zhen Prefecture; Song accompanied him as adjutant.

units.zh: 時推官李蕘掌書，崧見其起草不工，密謂掌事呂柔曰：「令公皇子，天下瞻望，至於尺牘往來，章表論列，稍須文理合宜。
units.en: The judicial officer Li Rao then handled correspondence, and Song, finding his drafts clumsy, quietly told the steward Lü Rou, "His Lordship is an imperial prince, the hope of the realm; whatever letters and memorials go out should at least be literate and apt.
units.literal: At the time the judicial officer Li Rao managed documents; Song saw that his drafting was unskilled and secretly told the steward Lü Rou: "His Lordship is an imperial prince, watched by all under Heaven; as for letters exchanged and memorials submitted, the prose ought at least to be literate and fitting.

units.zh: 李侍御起草，未能盡善。」
units.en: Censor Li's drafts are not quite up to the mark."
units.literal: Censor Li's drafts are not fully adequate."

units.zh: 呂曰：「公試代為之。」
units.en: Lü replied, "Why don't you try drafting them yourself?"
units.literal: Lü said: "Sir, try drafting them yourself."

units.zh: 呂得崧所作，示盧質、馮道，皆稱之。
units.en: Lü took what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao, and both praised it.
units.literal: Lü obtained what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao; both praised it.

units.zh: 繇是擢為興聖宮巡官，獨掌奏記。
units.en: On that account he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and given sole charge of memorials and reports.
units.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and alone managed memorials and reports.

units.zh: 莊宗入洛，授太常寺協律郎。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was made harmonizing officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was appointed harmonizing officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 王師伐蜀，繼岌為都統，以崧掌書記。
units.en: When the imperial forces marched against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as his chief secretary.
units.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as chief secretary.

units.zh: 蜀平，樞密使郭崇韜為宦官誣構，繼岌遂殺崇韜父子，外尚未知。
units.en: After Shu fell, eunuchs framed Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Chongtao, and Jiji killed Chongtao and his son; the news had not yet spread beyond their camp.
units.literal: After Shu was pacified, the eunuchs slandered the Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao, and Jiji thereupon killed Chongtao and his son; those outside still did not know.

units.zh: 崧白繼岌曰：「王何為作此危事？
units.en: Song said to Jiji, "Your Highness, why do this reckless thing?
units.literal: Song told Jiji: "Your Highness, why commit this perilous act?

units.zh: 至於不容崇韜，至洛誅之未晚。
units.en: If Chongtao cannot be tolerated, you could still put him to death after you reach Luoyang.
units.literal: As for not tolerating Chongtao, it would not be too late to execute him after reaching Luoyang.

units.zh: 今懸軍五千里，無咫尺書詔，便殺重臣，非謀也。」
units.en: Your army is five thousand li from home with no word from the throne, yet you have killed a great minister—that is no sound policy."
units.literal: Now the army is isolated five thousand li away, without the slightest imperial edict, yet a great minister is killed—this is not sound planning."

units.zh: 繼岌曰：「吾亦悔之。」
units.en: Jiji said, "I regret it as well."
units.literal: Jiji said: "I too regret it."

units.zh: 崧召書吏三四人，登樓去梯，取黃紙矯寫詔書，倒使都統印發之。
units.en: Song called three or four clerks, had them climb a tower and pull up the ladder, forged an edict on yellow paper, and had it issued with the overall commander's seal impressed upside down.
units.literal: Song summoned three or four clerks, went up a tower and removed the ladder, took yellow paper and forged an edict, and had the overall commander's seal impressed upside down to issue it.

units.zh: 翌日，告諸軍，軍情稍定。
units.en: The next day he announced it to the troops, and army morale gradually settled.
units.literal: The next day he announced it to the armies, and morale gradually steadied.

units.zh: 及自蜀還，明宗革命，任圜以宰相判三司，用崧為鹽鐵推官，賜緋。
units.en: After the return from Shu, Emperor Mingzong took the throne; Ren Huan, serving as chancellor in charge of the Three Departments, appointed Song salt-and-iron investigating officer and gave him crimson robes.
units.literal: When he returned from Shu, Emperor Mingzong seized power; Ren Huan, as chancellor overseeing the Three Departments, employed Song as salt and iron investigating officer and granted him crimson robes.

units.zh: 丁內艱，歸鄉里。
units.en: When his mother died he went into mourning and returned home.
units.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and returned to his home district.

units.zh: 服闋，鎮帥範延光奏署掌書記。
units.en: After mourning he was appointed chief secretary on Fan Yanguang's recommendation as military governor.
units.literal: When mourning ended, the military governor Fan Yanguang memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.

units.zh: 延光為樞密使，拜拾遺，直樞密院，遷補闕、起居郎、尚書郎，充職如故。
units.en: When Yanguang became military affairs commissioner, Song was made remonstrance official and attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs; he rose through censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretariat posts while keeping his original duties.
units.literal: When Yanguang became Commissioner of Military Affairs, Song was appointed remonstrance official and served in the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was promoted to censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretary in the Secretariat, while continuing in his duties as before.

units.zh: 長興末，改翰林學士。
units.en: Near the end of the Changxing reign he was made a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he was made Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 清泰初，拜端明殿學士、戶部侍郎。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai reign he was made Duanming Hall academician and vice minister of revenue.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue.

units.zh: 先是，長興三年冬，契丹入雲中，朝廷欲命重將鎮太原。
units.en: Earlier, in the winter of Changxing year three, the Khitans entered Yunzhong, and the court wanted a senior general posted to Taiyuan.
units.literal: Earlier, in the winter of the third year of Changxing, the Khitan entered Yunzhong, and the court wished to appoint a weighty general to guard Taiyuan.

units.zh: 時晉祖為六軍副使，以秦王從榮不軌，懇求外任，深有北門之望，而大臣以晉高祖方權兵柄，難以議之。
units.en: The future Jin founder was then deputy commander of the Six Armies; with Li Congrong, Prince of Qin, plotting treason, he urgently sought a post away from court and dearly hoped for the northern command, yet the senior ministers, knowing he already held the armies, hesitated to broach the appointment.
units.literal: At the time the Jin founder was deputy commander of the Six Armies; because Li Congrong, Prince of Qin, was disloyal, he earnestly sought an outside post and deeply hoped for the northern command, but the great ministers, since the Jin founder already held military power, found it hard to discuss the matter.

units.zh: 一日，明宗怒其未奏，範延光、趙延壽等無對，退歸本院，共議其事，方欲以康義誠為之。
units.en: One day Mingzong, furious that no memorial had come in, got no answer from Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and the others; they withdrew to their bureau, debated the post together, and were on the point of naming Kang Yicheng.
units.literal: One day Emperor Mingzong, angry that they had not memorialized, received no reply from Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and the rest; they withdrew to their bureau, discussed the matter together, and were about to appoint Kang Yicheng.

units.zh: 時崧最在下位，聳立請曰：「朝廷重兵多在北邊，須以重臣為帥，以某所見，非石太尉不可也。」
units.en: Song ranked lowest in the room; he stood up and said, "Most of the court's heavy troops are in the north—we need a senior minister in command, and in my view only Grand Marshal Shi will serve."
units.literal: Song was then lowest in rank; he stood erect and requested: "The court's main forces are mostly in the north; a weighty minister must command them—in my view none but Grand Marshal Shi will do."

units.zh: 會明宗令中使促之，眾乃從其議。
units.en: Just then Mingzong sent a palace envoy to hurry them along, and the group adopted Song's view.
units.literal: Just then Emperor Mingzong sent a palace envoy to press them, and the assembly followed his proposal.

units.zh: 翌日，晉祖既受太原之命，使心腹達意於崧云：「壘浮圖須與合卻尖。」
units.en: The next day, once the Jin founder had the Taiyuan appointment, he sent a confidant to tell Song, "When you raise a pagoda, the spire has to be set on top"—meaning Song had made his rise possible.
units.literal: The next day, after the Jin founder received the Taiyuan appointment, he had a confidant convey his meaning to Song: "When building a pagoda, the spire must be fitted on.

units.zh: 蓋感之深也。
units.en: So deep was his gratitude.
units.literal: This showed how deeply he was moved.

units.zh: 及清泰末，晉祖入洛，崧與呂琦俱竄匿於伊闕民家。
units.en: Late in Qingtai, when the Jin founder entered Luoyang, Song and Lü Qi went into hiding in a villager's home at Yique.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai, when the Jin founder entered Luoyang, Song and Lü Qi both fled and hid in a commoner's house at Yique.

units.zh: 旬日，晉高祖召為戶部侍郎，判戶部。
units.en: Within ten days Jin Gaozu summoned him back as vice minister of revenue in charge of the ministry.
units.literal: Within ten days the Jin Gaozu summoned him as vice minister of revenue to oversee the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 逾月，拜中書侍郎、同平章事，與桑維翰並兼樞密使。
units.en: A month later he was made vice director of the Secretariat, co-equal councilor of state, and shared the military affairs commission with Sang Weihan.
units.literal: After more than a month he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, co-equal councilor of state, and together with Sang Weihan concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 維翰鎮相州，未幾，廢樞密院，事歸中書，加尚書右僕射。
units.en: Weihan went to govern Xiang Prefecture; soon the military affairs bureau was abolished and its business reverted to the Secretariat, and Song was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: Weihan governed Xiang Prefecture; before long the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished and its affairs returned to the Secretariat; Song was further made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 從幸鄴，丁外艱，恩制起復，崧上章數四，懇辭其命，優詔不允。
units.en: While accompanying the emperor to Ye he lost his father; an edict recalled him from mourning, but Song memorialized four times to decline, and each gracious reply refused him.
units.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Ye, he entered mourning for his father; by gracious edict he was recalled to office; Song submitted memorials four times, earnestly declining the appointment, but favorable edicts would not allow it.

units.zh: 復上章，不報，崧不得已而視事。
units.en: He memorialized again without answer and at last took up office against his will.
units.literal: He memorialized again and received no reply; Song had no choice but to take up his duties.

units.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，復用桑維翰為樞密使，命崧兼判三司。
units.en: When the young Jin emperor succeeded, Sang Weihan was again military affairs commissioner, and Song was put in charge of the Three Departments as well.
units.literal: When the Jin young emperor succeeded, Sang Weihan was again made Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Song was ordered concurrently to oversee the Three Departments.

units.zh: 未幾，代維翰為樞密使，與馮玉對掌機密。
units.en: Soon he replaced Weihan as military affairs commissioner and shared confidential state business with Feng Yu.
units.literal: Before long he replaced Weihan as Commissioner of Military Affairs and with Feng Yu jointly held confidential affairs.

units.zh: 開運末，崧、玉信契丹之詐，經略瀛、鄭，中渡之敗，落其奸謀。
units.en: Late in Kaiyun, Song and Yu trusted Khitan promises, directed operations at Ying and Zheng, and at the Zhongdu rout walked into their trap.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, Song and Yu trusted the Khitan deception, planned operations at Ying and Zheng, and at the defeat at Zhongdu fell into their treacherous scheme.

units.zh: 契丹入京師，趙延壽、張礪素稱崧之才，契丹主善遇之，以崧為太子太師，充樞密使。
units.en: When the Khitans took the capital, Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li had long praised Song's ability; the Khitan ruler treated him kindly, made him grand preceptor of the heir apparent, and kept him as military affairs commissioner.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered the capital, Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li had long praised Song's talent; the Khitan ruler treated him well, made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and kept him as Commissioner of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 契丹主嘗謂左右曰：「我破南朝，只得李崧一人而已。」
units.en: The Khitan ruler once told his attendants, "In conquering the southern dynasty I have won only Li Song."
units.literal: The Khitan ruler once told those around him: "In conquering the Southern Court I have gained only Li Song."

units.zh: 從契丹北行，留於鎮州。
units.en: He started north with the Khitans but was left behind at Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: He followed the Khitan northward but was left at Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 高祖平汴、洛，乃以崧之居第賜蘇逢吉，第中宿藏之物，皆為逢吉所有。
units.en: After Gaozu pacified Bian and Luoyang, he gave Song's house to Su Fengji, along with everything Song had kept there.
units.literal: When the Gaozu pacified Bian and Luo, he bestowed Song's residence on Su Fengji, and everything stored in the house became Fengji's.

units.zh: 是年秋，鎮州逐麻答，崧與馮道、和凝十數人歸闕，授太子太傅。
units.en: That autumn Zhen Prefecture expelled Maduo; Song returned to court with Feng Dao, He Ning, and a dozen others and was made grand tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: That autumn Zhen Prefecture drove out Maduo; Song returned to court with Feng Dao, He Ning, and more than ten others and was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 崧對朝之權右，謙挹承顏，未嘗忤旨。
units.en: Though powerful at court, Song was humble and obliging before the throne and never crossed the emperor.
units.literal: Song, though powerful at court, was modest and deferential in bearing and never went against the emperor's will.

units.zh: 嘗以宅券獻蘇逢吉，不悅。
units.en: He once offered Su Fengji the deed to his former house, and Fengji took offense.
units.literal: He once presented the deed to his house to Su Fengji, who was displeased.

units.zh: 崧二弟嶼、㠖，酣酒無識，與楊邠、蘇逢吉子弟杯酒之間，時言及奪我居第，逢吉知之。
units.en: Song's younger brothers Yu and Xiu, drunken and rash, would complain over wine with the sons of Yang Bin and Su Fengji that their home had been taken; Fengji heard of it.
units.literal: Song's two younger brothers Yu and Xiu, given to drunkenness and without judgment, at drinking with the sons of Yang Bin and Su Fengji sometimes spoke of having their residence seized; Fengji learned of it.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·陶蒨傳》：李崧以宅券獻逢吉，逢吉不悅，而崧子弟數出怨言，崧懼，移疾不出。
units.en: (History of Song, Biography of Tao Qian: Li Song gave Fengji the deed to his house; Fengji was offended, while Song's sons and nephews kept voicing grievances, so Song, afraid, pleaded illness and stayed away from court.)
units.literal: (From the Biography of Tao Qian in the History of Song: Li Song presented the house deed to Fengji, and Fengji was displeased; Song's sons and nephews often uttered complaints, and Song, in fear, pleaded illness and did not go out.)

units.zh: 崧族子昉，嘗往候崧，崧語昉曰：「邇來朝廷於我有何議？」
units.en: Song's kinsman Fang once called on him, and Song asked, "Has the court been saying anything about me lately?"
units.literal: Song's clansman Fang once went to visit him; Song said to Fang: "Of late has the court had any discussion concerning me?"

units.zh: 昉曰：「無他，聞唯陶給事往往於稠人中厚誣叔父。」
units.en: Fang said, "Nothing else—only that Attendant Tao often speaks harshly against you in public gatherings."
units.literal: Fang said: "Nothing else—I hear only that Attendant Tao often slanders my uncle harshly in crowded gatherings."

units.zh: 崧嘆曰：「蒨自單州判官，吾取為集賢校理，不數年擢掌詔命，吾何負於陶氏子哉！」
units.en: Song sighed, "Qian was only a Shan prefecture judge when I brought him into the Hall of Assembled Worthies; within a few years I had him drafting edicts—what did I ever do to that Tao boy?"
units.literal: Song sighed and said: "Qian began as judge of Shan Prefecture; I took him as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and within a few years promoted him to draft edicts—what have I done to wrong the son of the Tao family!"

units.zh: 及崧遇禍，昉嘗因公事詣蒨，蒨問昉：「識李侍郎否？」
units.en: After Song's fall, Fang once visited Qian on business; Qian asked, "Do you know Vice Director Li?"
units.literal: When Song met disaster, Fang once went to Qian on official business; Qian asked Fang: "Do you know Vice Director Li?"

units.zh: 昉斂衽應曰：「遠從叔耳。」
units.en: Fang straightened his robe and answered, "My distant uncle."
units.literal: Fang straightened his robe and replied: "He is my distant uncle."

units.zh: 蒨曰：「李氏之禍，蒨出力焉。」
units.en: Qian said, "I had a hand in the Li family's ruin."
units.literal: Qian said: "In the Li family's calamity, Qian exerted his strength."

units.zh: 昉聞之汗出。）〉
units.en: Fang broke into a sweat at the words.)〉
units.literal: Hearing this, Fang broke into a sweat.)〉

units.zh: 有部曲葛延遇者，逋李嶼船傭，嶼撻之，督其所負，遇有同輩李澄亦事逢吉，葛延遇夜寄宿於澄家，以嶼見督情告，遂一夕同謀告變。
units.en: A retainer named Ge Yanyu owed Li Yu for boat hire; Yu beat him and demanded payment. Yanyu had a fellow named Li Cheng who also served Fengji; one night Ge stayed at Cheng's house, told him how Yu had hounded him, and that night the two plotted to accuse the Li family of treason.
units.literal: There was a retainer Ge Yanyu who owed Li Yu for boat hire; Yu flogged him and pressed for what was owed. Yanyu had a comrade Li Cheng who also served Fengji; Ge Yanyu lodged at Cheng's house one night, told him how Yu had pressed him, and in one night they plotted together to report treason.

units.zh: 逢吉覽狀示史宏肇，其日逢吉遣吏召崧至第，從容語及葛延遇告變之事，崧以幼女為托，逢吉遣吏送於侍衛獄。
units.en: Fengji read the accusation and showed it to Shi Hongzhao; that day he sent clerks to bring Song to his house, mentioned Ge Yanyu's treason report in an easy tone, took Song's plea for his young daughter, and had clerks escort him to the guards' prison.
units.literal: Fengji read the report and showed it to Shi Hongzhao; that day Fengji sent clerks to summon Song to his residence, spoke calmly of Ge Yanyu's report of treason, Song entrusted his young daughter to him, and Fengji sent clerks to convey him to the guards' prison.

units.zh: 既行，崧恚曰：「自古未有不亡之國，不死之人。」
units.en: As he was led away, Song said bitterly, "Since antiquity no state has failed to fall and no man has escaped death."
units.literal: As he went, Song said in anger: "Since antiquity there has never been a state that did not perish or a person who did not die."

units.zh: 及為吏所鞫，乃自誣伏罪，舉家遇害，少長悉屍於市，人士冤之。
units.en: Under interrogation he falsely confessed; his whole family was killed, young and old left dead in the market, and men of letters called it a gross injustice.
units.literal: When interrogated by the clerks, he falsely confessed guilt; the whole family suffered, young and old alike left corpses in the market, and scholars deemed it unjust.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·王溥傳》：世宗嘗問：「漢相李崧蠟彈書結契丹，有記其詞者否？」
units.en: (Brief Account of the Eastern Capital, Biography of Wang Pu: Emperor Shizong once asked, "Did the Han chancellor Li Song use a wax-sealed letter to ally with the Khitans—is there any record of what it said?"
units.literal: (From the Biography of Wang Pu in the Brief Account of the Eastern Capital: Emperor Shizong once asked: "Did Han chancellor Li Song use a wax-sealed letter to ally with the Khitan—is there any record of its wording?"

units.zh: 溥曰：「崧有此，肯示人耶？
units.en: Pu said, "If Song had done that, would he have let anyone see it?
units.literal: Pu said: "If Song had such a thing, would he show it to anyone?

units.zh: 蘇逢吉輩陷之爾。」
units.en: Su Fengji and his crowd framed him, that is all."
units.literal: Su Fengji and his ilk framed him, that is all."

units.zh: 世宗遂優贈崧官。）〉
units.en: Shizong then posthumously restored Song's honors.)〉
units.literal: Thereupon Shizong generously posthumously promoted Song's office.)〉

units.zh: 崧與徐臺符同學相善，乾祐三年秋，臺符夢崧謂曰：「予之冤橫，得請於帝矣。」
units.en: Song and Xu Taifu had been classmates and close friends; in the autumn of Qianyou year three, Taifu dreamed that Song told him, "My grievous wrong will now be heard in Heaven."
units.literal: Song and Xu Taifu had been schoolmates and were close; in the autumn of the third year of Qianyou, Taifu dreamed that Song told him: "My grievous wrong has obtained a hearing from the emperor."

units.zh: 及蘇、史之誅，並梟首於市，當崧所誅之地。
units.en: When Su and Shi were executed, their heads were displayed in the market at the very spot where Song had died.
units.literal: When Su and Shi were executed, their heads were displayed in the market at the very place where Song had been put to death.

units.zh: 未幾，葛延遇、李澄亦以戮死。
units.en: Soon Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng were executed as well.
units.literal: Before long Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng also died by execution.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·李昉傳》：晉侍中崧，與昉同宗且同里，時人謂崧為「東李家」，昉為「西李」。
units.en: (History of Song, Biography of Li Fang: Jin palace attendant Song was Fang's clansman and fellow townsman; people called Song "the eastern Li" and Fang "the western Li.")
units.literal: (From the Biography of Li Fang in the History of Song: Jin Palace Attendant Song was of the same clan and native place as Fang; people of the time called Song "the eastern Li family" and Fang "the western Li.")

units.zh: 漢末，崧被誅，至宋，其子璨自蘇州常熟縣令赴調，昉為訟其父冤，且言周太祖已為昭雪，贈官，還其田宅，錄璨而官之。
units.en: At the end of Later Han, Song was executed; under the Song his son Can came up from magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to the capital; Fang pleaded his father's case, noting that Zhou Taizu had already cleared Song's name, restored his rank, returned his lands and house, and enrolled Can in office.
units.literal: At the end of Han, Song was executed; in Song times his son Can came from magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to take the capital examination; Fang pleaded his father's injustice, saying that Zhou Taizu had already cleared his name, restored his office, and returned his fields and house, and had enrolled Can and given him office.

units.zh: 然璨幾五十，尚淹州縣之職。
units.en: Yet Can was nearly fifty and still held only a county post.
units.literal: Yet Can was nearly fifty and still stuck in prefectural and county posts.

units.zh: 詔授璨著作佐郎，後官至資善大夫。）〉
units.en: An edict made Can an assistant in the Bureau of Authorship; he later rose to grand master for the heir apparent's studies.)〉
units.literal: An edict appointed Can assistant in the Bureau of Authorship; he later reached the office of Grand Master for the Heir Apparent's Studies.)〉

units.zh: 蘇逢吉，長安人。
units.en: Su Fengji was a native of Chang'an.
units.literal: Su Fengji was a native of Chang'an.

units.zh: 父悅，逢吉母早喪，而悅鰥居，旁無侍者。
units.en: His father Yue lost Fengji's mother early and lived alone as a widower with no one to wait on him.
units.literal: His father was Yue; Fengji's mother died early, and Yue lived as a widower with no attendants at his side.

units.zh: 性嗜酒，雖所飲不多，然漱醪終日。
units.en: He loved wine; though he drank little, he kept rinsing his mouth with fresh brew all day.
units.literal: By nature he loved wine; though he did not drink much, he rinsed his mouth with new wine all day long.

units.zh: 他人供膳，皆不稱旨，俟逢吉庖炙，方肯下箸。
units.en: Food others prepared never suited him; he would eat only after Fengji had cooked.
units.literal: Meals others provided never pleased him; he would use chopsticks only after Fengji had cooked.

units.zh: 悅初仕蜀，官升朝列，逢吉初學為文，嘗代父染翰。
units.en: Yue had first served Shu and risen to court rank; Fengji was learning to write and sometimes drafted documents for his father.
units.literal: Yue first served Shu and rose to court rank; Fengji was first learning to write and sometimes drafted for his father.

units.zh: 悅嘗為高祖從事，甚見禮遇，因從容薦逢吉曰：「老夫耄矣，才器無取。
units.en: Yue had served Gaozu as an aide and was well treated; he casually recommended Fengji, saying, "I am old and have no talent worth offering.
units.literal: Yue had once been an aide to the Gaozu and was greatly honored; he therefore casually recommended Fengji, saying: "This old man is senile and without talent worth taking.

units.zh: 男逢吉粗學援毫，性復恭恪，如公不以犭屯犬之微，願令事左右。」
units.en: My son Fengji has some schooling with the brush and a respectful nature; if you would not scorn this worthless fellow, I ask that he serve at your side."
units.literal: My son Fengji has rough learning with the brush and a respectful, careful nature; if Your Lordship does not disdain this pig-dog's slight worth, I wish to have him serve at your side."

units.zh: 高祖召見，以神精爽惠，甚憐之。
units.en: Gaozu summoned him, found him bright and quick-witted, and took a strong liking to him.
units.literal: The Gaozu summoned him and, finding his spirit bright and quick-witted, greatly favored him.

units.zh: 有頃，擢為賓佐，凡有謀議，立侍其側。
units.en: Soon he was promoted to staff adviser and stood at Gaozu's side whenever counsel was needed.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to staff adviser; whenever there was counsel to be given, he stood at the Gaozu's side.

units.zh: 高祖素嚴毅，及鎮太原，位望崇重，從事稀得謁見，惟逢吉日侍左右。
units.en: Gaozu had always been stern; posted to Taiyuan with high rank and prestige, his aides rarely saw him—only Fengji attended him day after day.
units.literal: The Gaozu had always been stern and austere; when he governed Taiyuan his position and prestige were lofty, and aides rarely gained audience—only Fengji attended him daily at his side.

units.zh: 兩使文簿，堆案盈幾，左右不敢輒通，逢吉置於懷袖，俟其悅色則諮之，多見其可。
units.en: Papers from the two commissioners piled his desk high; attendants dared not pass them in, but Fengji slipped them into his sleeve and, when Gaozu was in good humor, presented them—most won approval.
units.literal: Documents from the two commissioners piled the desk full; those at his side dared not pass them through, but Fengji tucked them in his sleeve and, waiting until the Gaozu was in good humor, consulted him—most were approved.

units.zh: 高祖建號於太原，逢吉自節度判官拜同平章事、集賢殿大學士。
units.en: When Gaozu proclaimed his reign at Taiyuan, Fengji rose from military governor's judge to co-equal councilor and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
units.literal: When the Gaozu established his reign title at Taiyuan, Fengji rose from military governor's judge to co-equal councilor of state and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

units.zh: 車駕至汴，朝廷百司庶務，逢吉以為己任，參決處置，並出胸臆，雖有當有否，而事無留滯。
units.en: When the court reached Bian, Fengji took charge of the hundred offices' business; he decided everything from his own judgment—right or wrong—and nothing stalled.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bian, Fengji took all the hundred offices' routine affairs of the court as his charge; he joined in deciding and disposing of them, all from his own breast—though some were right and some wrong, nothing was held up.

units.zh: 會翰林學士李濤從容侍帝，言及霸府二相，官秩未崇，逢吉旋加吏部尚書，未幾，轉左僕射，監修國史。
units.en: When Hanlin academician Li Tao, attending the emperor casually, remarked that the two chancellors from the hegemonic headquarters were not yet high in rank, Fengji was promptly made minister of personnel; soon he became left vice director and oversaw the national history.
units.literal: When Hanlin academician Li Tao attended the emperor at ease and spoke of the two chancellors of the hegemonic headquarters, whose ranks were not yet exalted, Fengji was promptly made minister of personnel; before long he was transferred to left vice director and supervised compilation of the national history.

units.zh: 從征杜重威於鄴下，數乘醉抵辱周太祖。
units.en: On the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye, he repeatedly insulted the future Zhou Taizu while drunk.
units.literal: On the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye, he several times, drunk, insulted the Zhou Taizu.

units.zh: 及高祖大漸，與楊邠、史宏肇等臥內同受顧命。
units.en: When Gaozu fell gravely ill, he received the dying charge in the inner chamber along with Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the others.
units.literal: When the Gaozu fell gravely ill, he with Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest received the dying charge together in the inner chamber.

units.zh: 李濤與逢吉論甥舅之契，相得甚歡，濤之入相，逢吉甚有力焉。
units.en: Li Tao and Fengji were related as nephew and uncle by marriage and were on excellent terms; Fengji had done much to put Tao in the chancellorship.
units.literal: Li Tao and Fengji were linked as nephew and uncle by marriage and got on very well; Fengji had great influence in Tao's entering the chancellorship.

units.zh: 會濤上章，請出兩樞密為方鎮，帝怒，罷濤相，勒歸私第，時論疑濤承逢吉之風旨。
units.en: When Tao memorialized to send the two military commissioners out as regional governors, the emperor was furious, stripped him of the chancellorship, and sent him home; contemporaries suspected he was acting on Fengji's cue.
units.literal: When Tao memorialized asking that the two military commissioners be sent out as regional governors, the emperor was angry, removed Tao from the chancellorship, and ordered him back to his private residence; opinion at the time suspected Tao of following Fengji's intent.

units.zh: 先是，高祖踐阼之後，逢吉與蘇禹珪俱在中書，有所除拜，多違舊制，用舍升降，率意任情，至有自白丁而升宦路、由流外而除令錄者，不可勝數。
units.en: Earlier, after Gaozu took the throne, Fengji and Su Yugui sat in the Secretariat and often broke precedent in appointments, promoting and demoting at whim—even elevating commoners to office and outsiders to magistracies beyond number.
units.literal: Earlier, after the Gaozu took the throne, Fengji and Su Yugui were both in the Secretariat; in appointments and dismissals they often violated old regulations, promoting and demoting at will, so that there were those who rose from commoner status into office and from outside the regular stream who were made magistrates and recorders—beyond counting.

units.zh: 物論紛然。
units.en: Public opinion was in uproar.
units.literal: Public opinion was in uproar.

units.zh: 高祖方倚信二相，莫敢言者。
units.en: Gaozu still trusted the two chancellors, and no one dared object.
units.literal: The Gaozu was then relying on the two chancellors, and none dared speak.

units.zh: 逢吉尤貪財貨，無所顧避，求進之士，稍有物力者，即遣人微露風旨，許以美秩。
units.en: Fengji was especially greedy and unscrupulous; anyone seeking office who had even modest wealth would get a subtle hint and a promise of a fine post.
units.literal: Fengji was especially greedy for wealth and shrank from nothing; for those seeking advancement who had even slight means, he sent men to hint subtly and promised fine ranks.

units.zh: 及楊邠為相，稍奪二蘇之權，自是盡斂手而已。
units.en: When Yang Bin became chancellor, he gradually stripped the two Sus of power, and from then on they could only keep their hands in their sleeves.
units.literal: When Yang Bin became chancellor, he gradually stripped the two Sus of power; from then on they only held back their hands.

units.zh: 邠每懲二蘇之失，艱於除拜，至於諸司補吏，與門胄出身，一切停罷。
units.en: Each time Yang Bin punished the two Sus for their abuses he tightened appointments—even routine clerkships and posts gained by family pedigree were stopped entirely.
units.literal: Bin each time punished the two Sus for their faults and was strict about appointments; even clerks in the various offices and those entering office by family pedigree were all halted.

units.zh: 時論以邠之蔽，固亦由逢吉、禹珪本不能至公於物之所致也。
units.en: Public opinion held that Bin's excess was also because Fengji and Yugui had never been fair in the first place.
units.literal: Opinion held that Bin's obstruction was also caused by Fengji and Yugui being fundamentally unable to be fair toward others.

units.zh: 初，高祖至汴，以故相馮道、李崧為契丹所俘，佇於真定，乃以崧第賜逢吉，道第賜禹珪，崧於西洛有別業，亦為逢吉所有。
units.en: When Gaozu first reached Bian, former chancellors Feng Dao and Li Song, held by the Khitans at Zhending, were still away; he gave Song's house to Fengji and Dao's to Yugui, and Song's estate in western Luoyang went to Fengji as well.
units.literal: Earlier, when the Gaozu reached Bian, the former chancellors Feng Dao and Li Song had been captured by the Khitan and detained at Zhending; he gave Song's residence to Fengji and Dao's to Yugui; Song also had a separate estate in western Luo, which Fengji likewise took.

units.zh: 及真定逐契丹，崧、道歸朝，崧弟嶼以逢吉占據其第，時出怨言。
units.en: After Zhending expelled the Khitans, Song and Dao returned; Song's brother Yu, whose house Fengji still held, sometimes complained openly.
units.literal: When Zhending drove out the Khitan, Song and Dao returned to court; Song's brother Yu, because Fengji occupied his residence, at times uttered complaints.

units.zh: 未幾，崧以西京宅券獻於逢吉，不悅。
units.en: Soon Song offered Fengji the deed to his western capital property, and Fengji took offense.
units.literal: Before long Song presented the western capital house deed to Fengji, who was displeased.

units.zh: 會崧有仆夫欲誣告謀反，逢吉誘致其狀，即告史宏肇，令逮捕其家。
units.en: When one of Song's servants tried to frame him for treason, Fengji drew out a written accusation, reported it to Shi Hongzhao, and had the whole household arrested.
units.literal: When Song had a servant who wished to accuse him of plotting rebellion, Fengji induced him to produce a written statement and at once reported to Shi Hongzhao, ordering the arrest of Song's household.

units.zh: 逢吉遣直省吏召崧至第，即令監至侍衛獄。
units.en: Fengji sent a secretariat clerk to bring Song to his house and at once had him placed in the guards' prison.
units.literal: Fengji sent a direct secretariat clerk to summon Song to his residence and immediately had him escorted to the guards' prison.

units.zh: 翌日，所司以獄辭上，其李嶼款招云：「與兄崧、弟鳷，與家僮二十人商議，比至山陵發引之時，同放火謀亂，其告是實。」
units.en: The next day the authorities filed the confession; Li Yu's statement read, "My brother Song, my brother Zhi, and I, with twenty household slaves, agreed to set fires and raise rebellion when the tomb procession departed—this report is true."
units.literal: The next day the office submitted the prison confession; Li Yu's confession stated: "With my elder brother Song and younger brother Zhi, and twenty household slaves, we plotted that when the imperial tomb procession set out we would together set fires and rebel—the report is true."

units.zh: 蓋自誣之辭也。
units.en: It was plainly a forced confession.
units.literal: This was plainly a false confession.

units.zh: 逢吉仍以筆添註「二十人」字為「五十人」，封下有司，盡誅崧家。
units.en: Fengji altered "twenty men" to "fifty men" in the document, sealed it, and sent it down; the offices put Song's entire family to death.
units.literal: Fengji still used his brush to change the characters "twenty men" to "fifty men," sealed it, and sent it down to the offices, who executed Song's entire family.

units.zh: 時人冤之，歸咎於逢吉。
units.en: The people called it unjust and laid the blame on Fengji.
units.literal: People deemed it unjust and blamed Fengji.

units.zh: 逢吉深文好殺，從高祖在太原時，嘗因事，高祖命逢吉靜獄，以祈福祐，逢吉盡殺禁囚以報。
units.en: Fengji loved harsh laws and bloodshed; at Taiyuan with Gaozu, when ordered to "quiet the prisons" for a blessing, he killed every prisoner to report the task done.
units.literal: Fengji loved harsh laws and killing; when he followed the Gaozu at Taiyuan, on one occasion the Gaozu ordered Fengji to quiet the prisons to seek blessing; Fengji killed all the prisoners in confinement to report completion.

units.zh: 及執朝政，尤愛刑戮。
units.en: In power he especially favored punishments and executions.
units.literal: When he held court power he especially loved punishments and executions.

units.zh: 朝廷患諸處盜賊，遣使捕逐，逢吉自草詔意云：「應有賊盜，其本家及四鄰同保人，並仰所在全族處斬。」
units.en: With bandits troubling the realm, Fengji drafted an edict: "Wherever bandits appear, their families and four neighboring guarantors shall all be put to death by local authorities."
units.literal: The court was troubled by bandits everywhere and sent envoys to pursue them; Fengji himself drafted the edict's intent: "Wherever there are bandits, their original families and the four neighboring guarantors shall all be executed in full clan punishment by the local authorities."

units.zh: 或謂逢吉曰：「為盜者族誅，猶非王法，鄰保同罪，不亦甚乎？」
units.en: Someone told Fengji, "Clan execution for thieves is not royal law; punishing guarantors alike—is that not extreme?"
units.literal: Someone said to Fengji: "Executing the bandit's clan is still not royal law; punishing the guarantors alike—is that not excessive?"

units.zh: 逢吉堅以為是，竟去「全族」二字。
units.en: Fengji insisted he was right and finally struck only the words "full clan."
units.literal: Fengji insisted he was right and in the end removed only the two characters "full clan."

units.zh: 時有鄆州捕賊使臣張令柔盡殺平陰縣十七村民，良由此也。
units.en: The Yun prefecture bandit-hunter Zhang Lingrou then killed seventeen villagers of Pingyin County—because of this edict.
units.literal: At the time the bandit-catching envoy Zhang Lingrou of Yun Prefecture killed seventeen villagers of Pingyin County—this was precisely because of this.

units.zh: 逢吉性侈靡，好鮮衣美食，中書供膳，鄙而不食，私庖供饌，務盡甘珍。
units.en: Extravagant by nature, he loved fine dress and food, scorned the Secretariat's table, and had his private kitchen serve only the richest fare.
units.literal: Fengji was extravagant by nature, loving fine clothes and food; he disdained and would not eat the Secretariat's provisions, having his private kitchen supply delicacies to the utmost.

units.zh: 嘗於私第大張酒樂以召權貴，所費千餘緡。
units.en: Once at his home he threw a lavish feast for the powerful that cost more than a thousand strings of cash.
units.literal: He once at his private residence held a great feast with music to summon the powerful, costing more than a thousand strings of cash.

units.zh: 其妻武氏卒，葬送甚盛，班行官及外州節制，有與逢吉相款洽者，皆令賫送綾羅絹帛，以備縞素。
units.en: When his wife Lady Wu died, the funeral was lavish; every official and outer prefecture commissioner on good terms with him was told to send silk for mourning.
units.literal: When his wife the Lady Wu died, the funeral was very grand; officials in the procession and military commissioners of outer prefectures who were on good terms with Fengji were all ordered to send silk and cloth for mourning garments.

units.zh: 失禮違度，一至如此。
units.en: He violated ritual and exceeded all bounds of propriety.
units.literal: He violated ritual and exceeded propriety to this degree.

units.zh: 又性不拘名教，繼母死不行服，妻死未周，其子並授官秩。
units.en: He also scorned ritual propriety: he did not mourn his stepmother; before his wife had been dead a year, his sons received official ranks.
units.literal: He was also by nature unconstrained by the name of teaching: when his stepmother died he did not observe mourning; before a full year had passed since his wife's death, his sons were all given official ranks.

units.zh: 有庶兄自外至，不白逢吉，便見諸子，逢吉怒，且懼他日淩弱其子息，乃密白高祖，誣以他事杖殺之。
units.en: A half-brother arrived unannounced and visited his sons; Fengji, angry and fearing future harm to his children, secretly accused him to Gaozu and had him beaten to death on false charges.
units.literal: A half-brother came from outside without informing Fengji and went to see his sons; Fengji was angry and, fearing he would one day bully his children, secretly reported to the Gaozu and had him beaten to death on a trumped-up charge.

units.zh: 乾祐二年秋，加守司空。
units.en: In the autumn of Qianyou year two he was made acting minister of works.
units.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Qianyou he was further made acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 周太祖之將鎮鄴也，逢吉奏請落樞密使，隱帝曰：「有前例否？」
units.en: When the future Zhou Taizu was to take Ye, Fengji asked to strip him of the military commission; the Hidden Emperor asked, "Is there precedent?"
units.literal: When the Zhou Taizu was about to be posted to Ye, Fengji memorialized asking that he be removed as military commissioner; the Hidden Emperor said: "Is there a precedent?"

units.zh: 逢吉奏曰：「樞密之任，方鎮帶之非便。」
units.en: Fengji replied, "A regional commander should not also hold the military commission."
units.literal: Fengji memorialized: "The military commissioner's post is not convenient for a regional commander to hold concurrently."

units.zh: 史宏肇曰：「兼帶樞密，所冀諸軍稟畏。」
units.en: Shi Hongzhao said, "We want him to hold the commission so the armies will fear him."
units.literal: Shi Hongzhao said: "Holding the military commission concurrently is what we hope will make the armies stand in awe."

units.zh: 竟從宏肇之議。
units.en: They followed Hongzhao's view in the end.
units.literal: In the end they followed Hongzhao's proposal.

units.zh: 宏肇怨逢吉之異己，逢吉曰：「此國家之事也，且以內制外則順，以外制內豈得便耶！」
units.en: Hongzhao resented Fengji's dissent; Fengji said, "This is a state matter; inner rule over outer is proper—how can outer rule over inner be right?"
units.literal: Hongzhao resented Fengji for differing from him; Fengji said: "This is a matter of state; moreover, inner controlling outer is orderly—outer controlling inner, how can that be convenient!"

units.zh: 事雖不從，物議多之。
units.en: Though his view was rejected, public opinion largely sided with him.
units.literal: Though the matter was not adopted, public opinion largely approved.

units.zh: 居無何，王章張飲，會逢吉與史宏肇有謔言，大為宏肇所詬，逢吉不校，幾至毆擊，逢吉馳馬而歸，自是將相失歡。
units.en: Soon at Wang Zhang's banquet, banter between Fengji and Shi Hongzhao turned into fierce abuse; Fengji held his tongue and nearly came to blows, then galloped home—after that the chancellor and commissioner were estranged.
units.literal: Before long, at Wang Zhang's drinking party, Fengji and Shi Hongzhao exchanged banter that turned into Hongzhao's fierce reviling; Fengji did not answer back and nearly came to blows; Fengji galloped home—from then on chancellor and commissioner were estranged.

units.zh: 逢吉欲希外任，以紓宏肇之怒，既而中輟。
units.en: Fengji hoped for an outside post to appease Hongzhao, but soon gave it up.
units.literal: Fengji wished for an outside post to ease Hongzhao's anger, but soon dropped the idea.

units.zh: 人問其故，逢吉曰：「茍領一方鎮，只消得史公一處分。
units.en: Asked why, Fengji said, "If I held a regional command, one order from Lord Shi would be enough.
units.literal: When people asked why, Fengji said: "If I merely held one regional command, it would take only one order from Lord Shi.

units.zh: 則為齏粉矣。」
units.en: And I would be ground to dust."
units.literal: Then I would be reduced to powder."

units.zh: 李業輩惡宏肇、楊邠等，逢吉知之，每見業等，即微以言激怒之。
units.en: Li Ye's faction hated Hongzhao and Yang Bin; Fengji knew it and subtly goaded them whenever he met them.
units.literal: Li Ye and his faction hated Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the rest; Fengji knew this and whenever he saw Ye and the others would subtly provoke them with words.

units.zh: 及宏肇等被害，逢吉不預其謀，聞變驚駭，即受宣徽，權知樞密院事。
units.en: When Hongzhao and the others were killed, Fengji had not plotted it; shocked by the coup, he took the palace treasury post and acted as military commissioner.
units.literal: When Hongzhao and the others were killed, Fengji had not joined the plot; hearing the coup he was shocked, immediately accepted the Palace Treasury commission, and acted as military affairs commissioner.

units.zh: 尋令草制正授，制入，聞鄴兵至澶州乃止。
units.en: He was told to draft the formal appointment; when the draft was submitted, word that Ye's army had reached Chanzhou halted it.
units.literal: Soon he was ordered to draft the formal appointment; when the draft entered, news that Ye troops had reached Chanzhou stopped it.

units.zh: 事急，逢吉謂人曰：「蕭墻之變，太覺匆遽，主上若有一言見問，必不至是矣。」
units.en: In the crisis he said, "This palace upheaval came too suddenly; if the emperor had asked me one question, it would never have come to this."
units.literal: In the crisis Fengji told others: "This turmoil within the palace walls came far too suddenly; if the emperor had asked me a single question, it would never have come to this."

units.zh: 數夕宿於金祥殿之東，謂天官正王處訥曰：「夜來就枕未瞑，已見李崧在傍，生人與死人相接，無吉事也。」
units.en: For nights he lodged east of Jinxian Hall and told the chief astronomer Wang Chun'e, "Last night before sleep I saw Li Song beside me—the living meeting the dead bodes ill."
units.literal: For several nights he lodged east of the Jinxian Hall and said to the director of astronomy Wang Chun'e: "Last night, before sleep, I already saw Li Song at my side; the living meeting the dead—nothing auspicious."

units.zh: 及周太祖自鄴至汴，官軍敗於劉子陂，是夕逢吉宿於七里郊，與同舍痛飲，醉將自刎，左右止之。
units.en: When Zhou Taizu came from Ye to Bian and the army was beaten at Liuzi Slope, that night Fengji lodged at Qili, drank heavily with companions, and was stopped as he tried to kill himself.
units.literal: When the Zhou Taizu came from Ye to Bian and the imperial army was defeated at Liuzi Slope, that night Fengji lodged at Qili suburb and drank heavily with his companions; drunk, he was about to kill himself but attendants stopped him.

units.zh: 至曙，與隱帝同抵民舍，遂自殺。
units.en: At dawn he and the Hidden Emperor reached a commoner's house, and there he killed himself.
units.literal: At dawn he reached a commoner's house together with the Hidden Emperor and there killed himself.

units.zh: 周太祖定京城，與聶文進等同梟於北市，釋其家族。
units.en: When Zhou Taizu secured the capital, he and Nie Wenjin and others were displayed at the north market; their families were spared.
units.literal: When the Zhou Taizu secured the capital, he and Nie Wenjin and the rest were displayed at the north market; their clans were released.

units.zh: 其梟首之處，適當李崧冤死之地。
units.en: The display spot was exactly where Li Song had been unjustly executed.
units.literal: The place where their heads were displayed was exactly where Li Song had died unjustly.

units.zh: 廣順初，詔就西京賜其子莊宅各一區。
units.en: Early in Guangshun an edict gave each of his sons a mansion in the western capital.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun an edict granted each of his sons a mansion in the western capital.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：高祖在河東幕府，闕書記，朝廷除前進士丘廷敏為之，以高祖有異志，恐為所累，辭疾不赴，遂改蘇逢吉。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: At Hedong headquarters the secretariat was vacant; the court named the former jinshi Qiu Tingmin, who, fearing Gaozu's rebellion would implicate him, pleaded illness; Su Fengji was appointed instead.)
units.literal: (From the Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When the Gaozu was in the Hedong headquarters, the secretariat post was vacant; the court appointed the former jinshi Qiu Tingmin, who, fearing the Gaozu's rebellious intent would implicate him, pleaded illness and did not go; Su Fengji was appointed instead.

units.zh: 未幾，契丹南侵，高祖仗順而起，兵不血刃而天下定，逢吉以佐命功，自掌書記拜中書侍郎、平章事。
units.en: Soon the Khitans invaded; Gaozu rose in support of Shun and took the realm without bloodshed; Fengji, for aiding the founding, rose from chief secretary to vice director and councilor.
units.literal: Before long the Khitan invaded south; the Gaozu rose in support of Shun and, without bloodshed, settled the realm; Fengji, for his founding merit, rose from chief secretary to vice director of the Secretariat and councilor of state.

units.zh: 逾年，廷敏始選授鳳翔麟遊縣令。
units.en: More than a year later Tingmin was finally appointed magistrate of Linyou in Fengxiang.
units.literal: After more than a year Tingmin was finally appointed magistrate of Linyou in Fengxiang.

units.zh: 過堂之日，逢吉戲之，且撫所坐椅子曰：「合是長官坐，何故讓與鄙夫耶？」
units.en: On the day he passed the hall, Fengji teased him, patting his chair: "This seat should be yours—why yield it to a nobody?"
units.literal: On the day he passed the hall, Fengji teased him and patted the chair he sat in, saying: "This ought to be the senior official's seat—why yield it to a base fellow?"

units.zh: 廷敏遂漸悚而退。）〉
units.en: Tingmin withdrew, increasingly afraid.)〉
units.literal: Tingmin thereupon withdrew in growing fear.)〉

units.zh: 李鏻，唐宗屬也。
units.en: Li Lin was of the Tang imperial clan.
units.literal: Li Lin was of the Tang imperial clan.

units.zh: 父洎，韶州刺史。
units.en: His father Ji was prefect of Shao.
units.literal: His father Ji was prefect of Shao.

units.zh: 伯父湯，咸通中為給事中。
units.en: His elder uncle Tang had been an attendant in the Xiantong era.
units.literal: His elder uncle Tang, in the Xiantong era, was attendant.

units.zh: 懿宗除乳母楚國夫人婿為夏州刺史，湯封還制書，詔曰：「朕少失所親，若非楚國夫人鞠養，則無朕此身，雖非朝典，望卿放下，仍今後不得援以為例。」
units.en: Emperor Yizong made the wet nurse the Lady of Chu's son-in-law prefect of Xia; Tang returned the edict; the emperor wrote, "I lost my parents young; without the Lady of Chu's care I would not live; though not precedent, set this aside and cite it no more."
units.literal: Emperor Yizong appointed the wet nurse the Lady of Chu state's son-in-law as prefect of Xia; Tang returned the sealed edict; the edict said: "I lost my parents young; if not for the Lady of Chu state's nurturing, I would not have this body; though it is not court precedent, I hope you will set it aside, and hereafter it must not be cited as precedent."

units.zh: 湯乃奉詔，其諒直如此。
units.en: Tang obeyed—such was his blunt integrity.
units.literal: Tang then obeyed the edict—such was his straightforward integrity.

units.zh: 鏻少舉進士，累舉不第。
units.en: Lin took the jinshi examination repeatedly in youth and failed.
units.literal: Lin in youth took the jinshi examination and failed repeatedly.

units.zh: 客遊河朔，稱清海軍掌書記，謁定州王處直，不見禮。
units.en: As a guest in Hebei he styled himself chief secretary of the Qinghai Army and called on Wang Chuzhi of Ding, who slighted him.
units.literal: Traveling as a guest in Hebei, he called himself chief secretary of the Qinghai Army and called on Wang Chuzhi of Ding Prefecture, who did not treat him with courtesy.

units.zh: 鏻即脫綠被緋，入常山謁要人李宏規，以宗姓請兄事之，由是得進。
units.en: He shed his official robes, went to Changshan, called on Li Honggui as a clansman asking to serve him as elder brother, and thereby advanced.
units.literal: Lin then removed his green robe and crimson, entered Changshan, and called on the powerful Li Honggui, asking as a clansman to serve him as elder brother, and thereby advanced.

units.zh: 趙王镕辟為從事，镕卒，復為王德明賓客。
units.en: Wang Rong, Prince of Zhao, made him an aide; after Rong's death he served Wang Deming as guest.
units.literal: Wang Rong, Prince of Zhao, made him an aide; when Rong died, he again became guest of Wang Deming.

units.zh: 德明使鏻聘於唐莊宗，鏻密疏德明之罪，且言可圖之狀，莊宗嘉之。
units.en: Deming sent him on embassy to Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong; Lin secretly reported Deming's crimes and how he could be taken; Zhuangzong praised him.
units.literal: Deming sent Lin on a mission to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang; Lin secretly memorialized Deming's crimes and described how he could be taken; Zhuangzong praised this.

units.zh: 及常山平，以鏻為霸府支使。
units.en: When Changshan fell, Lin was made branch secretary at the hegemonic headquarters.
units.literal: When Changshan was pacified, Lin was made branch secretary of the hegemonic headquarters.

units.zh: 嘗從容請於莊宗曰：「鏻有四子，請誅之。」
units.en: He once casually asked Zhuangzong, "I have four sons—please execute them."
units.literal: He once casually asked Zhuangzong: "Lin has four sons—please execute them."

units.zh: 莊宗問其故，對曰：「此輩生於常山，稟勃亂之氣，不可留也。」
units.en: Zhuangzong asked why; he said, "Born in Changshan, they bear its turbulent spirit—they cannot be kept."
units.literal: Zhuangzong asked the reason; he replied: "These were born in Changshan and bear its turbulent air—they cannot be kept."

units.zh: 莊宗笑而止。
units.en: Zhuangzong laughed and refused.
units.literal: Zhuangzong laughed and stopped it.

units.zh: 同光初，授宗正卿，俄兼工部侍郎。
units.en: Early in Tongguang he was director of the imperial clan court and soon vice minister of works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed director of the imperial clan court and soon also vice minister of works.

units.zh: 常山有唐啟運陵，鏻受富民李守恭賂，署為陵臺令，守恭暴橫，為長吏所訴，按之以聞，鏻左授司農少卿，削金紫，未幾，出為河府副使。
units.en: Changshan holds the Tang Qiyun tomb; Lin took a bribe from Li Shougong and made him tomb magistrate; Shougong's violence was reported; Lin was demoted to vice minister of agriculture, stripped of gold and purple, then sent out as He prefecture deputy commissioner.
units.literal: Changshan has the Tang Qiyun tomb; Lin took a bribe from the wealthy Li Shougong and appointed him tomb platform magistrate; Shougong was violent and was reported by the chief official; investigated and reported up, Lin was demoted to vice minister of agriculture and stripped of gold and purple; before long he went out as deputy commissioner of the He prefecture.

units.zh: 明宗即位，歷兵部、戶部侍郎，工部、戶部尚書。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served as vice ministers of war and revenue and as ministers of works and revenue.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Lin served as vice minister of war, vice minister of revenue, minister of works, and minister of revenue.

units.zh: 長興中，以與明宗有舊，常貯入相之意，從容謂時相曰：「唐祚中興，宜敦敘宗室，才高者合居相位。
units.en: In Changxing, with old ties to Mingzong, he often hoped for the chancellorship and told the chancellors, "The Tang restoration should honor the clan; the able should hold the highest office.
units.literal: In Changxing, because of old ties with Mingzong, he often harbored intent to enter the chancellorship and casually told the chancellors: "The Tang restoration should honor the imperial clan; the talented ought to hold the highest office.

units.zh: 仆雖不才，曾事莊宗霸府，見今上於藩邸時。
units.en: Though I lack talent, I served Zhuangzong's headquarters and knew the present emperor in his princely days.
units.literal: Though I am without talent, I once served Zhuangzong's hegemonic headquarters and saw the present emperor in his princely residence.

units.zh: 家代重侯累相，靖安李氏，不在諸族之下；
units.en: For generations my house produced marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li are not beneath other clans;
units.literal: For generations my house produced heavy marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li family is not beneath the other clans;

units.zh: 論才較藝，何讓眾人。
units.en: in talent and skill, why should I yield to others?
units.literal: comparing talent and skill, why yield to others.

units.zh: 久置仆於朝行，諸君安乎？」
units.en: Keeping me so long in routine posts—are you at ease?"
units.literal: Long placing me in court ranks—are you gentlemen at ease?"

units.zh: 馮道、趙鳳每怒其僭。
units.en: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were angered each time by his presumption.
units.literal: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were each time angered by his presumption.

units.zh: 有頃，鏻因淮南細人言事，乃謂樞密使安重誨曰：「偽吳欲歸國久矣，若朝廷先遣使諭之，則旋踵而至矣。」
units.en: Soon, on a Huainan informer's report, he told An Chonghui, "Wu has long wished to submit; if the court sends an envoy, they will come at once."
units.literal: Before long, because of a petty man from Huainan reporting affairs, he told Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "False Wu has long wished to return to the state; if the court first sends an envoy to instruct them, they will come in a trice."

units.zh: 重誨然之，以玉帶與細人，令往淮南為信，久而不反，由是出鏻為兗州行軍司馬。
units.en: Chonghui agreed and gave the man a jade belt as envoy to Huainan; he never returned; Lin was sent out as Yan prefecture marching adjutant.
units.literal: Chonghui agreed, gave the petty man a jade belt to go to Huainan as envoy; he did not return for a long time; on that account Lin was sent out as marching adjutant of Yan Prefecture.

units.zh: 得代歸闕，復為戶部尚書，尋轉兵部尚書，有頃兼判太常卿事。
units.en: Returning to court he was again minister of revenue, soon minister of war, and before long acting director of imperial sacrifices.
units.literal: When his replacement returned to court, he was again minister of revenue, soon transferred to minister of war, and before long concurrently acted as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 嘗權典選部，銓綜失序，物論非之。
units.en: He once ran personnel selection; his judgments were disorderly and opinion condemned him.
units.literal: He once held selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel; his evaluation was disorderly and public opinion condemned it.

units.zh: 晉天福中，守太子少保。
units.en: In Jin's Tianfu era he was junior tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he held the post of junior tutor of the heir apparent.

units.zh: 開運中，遷太子太保。
units.en: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

units.zh: 高祖至闕，授守司徒，數月而卒，年八十八。
units.en: When Gaozu reached court he was made acting minister of works; he died several months later at eighty-eight.
units.literal: When the Gaozu reached court he was appointed acting Minister of Works; several months later he died at age eighty-eight.

units.zh: 詔贈太傅。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him grand tutor.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 龍敏，字欲訥，幽州永清人。
units.en: Long Min, styled Yun'e, was from Yongqing in You Prefecture.
units.literal: Long Min, styled Yun'e, was a native of Yongqing in You Prefecture.

units.zh: 少學為儒，仕鄉里為假掾。
units.en: In youth he studied Confucian learning and served his district as acting clerk.
units.literal: In youth he studied as a Confucian and served in his district as acting clerk.

units.zh: 劉守光不道，敏避地浮陽，會戴思遠渡河而南，乃從之。
units.en: Liu Shouguang was tyrannical; Min fled to Fuyang; when Dai Siyuan crossed south, he followed.
units.literal: Liu Shouguang was lawless; Min fled to Fuyang; when Dai Siyuan crossed the river south, he followed him.

units.zh: 鄉人周知裕仕梁為裨將，敏往依焉，知裕屢薦不調，敏丐遊都邑累年。
units.en: His townsman Zhou Zhiyu was a Liang adjutant; Min relied on him; Zhiyu recommended him in vain; Min begged to wander the capital for years.
units.literal: His townsman Zhou Zhiyu served Liang as adjutant; Min went to rely on him; Zhiyu recommended him repeatedly without success; Min begged to wander the capital for years.

units.zh: 唐莊宗定魏博，敏聞故人馮道為霸府記室，乃客於河中，歲歸太原，館於馮道之家，監軍使張承業即署敏為巡官，典監軍奏記。
units.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Min heard Feng Dao was chief secretary; he lodged in Hedong, yearly visiting Taiyuan and staying with Feng Dao; Zhang Chengye appointed him touring officer in charge of memorials.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Min heard his old acquaintance Feng Dao was chief secretary of the hegemonic headquarters; he lodged in Hedong, each year returning to Taiyuan and staying at Feng Dao's house; Military Affairs Overseer Zhang Chengye then appointed Min touring officer, in charge of the overseer's memorials.

units.zh: 莊宗平河、洛，征為司門員外郎，以家貧乏養，求為興唐少尹。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the Yellow and Luo region, Min was summoned as vice director of the gate office; poor and unable to support his family, he asked to be vice governor of Xingtang.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified the Yellow and Luo rivers, Min was summoned as vice director of the Gate Office; because his family was poor and he lacked support, he asked to be vice governor of Xingtang.

units.zh: 逾年，丁母喪，退居鄴下，會趙在禮據鄴城，以敏鄉人，強起令署事，又為亂軍所迫，敏不敢拒。
units.en: A year later his mother died; he retired to Ye; Zhao Zaili, holding Ye, forced the townsman Min to serve; mutinous troops compelled him and he dared not refuse.
units.literal: After more than a year his mother died; he retired to Ye; when Zhao Zaili held Ye, because Min was a townsman, he was forcibly raised to serve; he was also compelled by the mutinous troops and dared not refuse.

units.zh: 明年，在禮鎮浮陽，敏復居喪制，服闋，除戶部郎中，改諫議大夫、御史中丞。
units.en: The next year Zaili governed Fuyang; Min mourned again; after mourning he was director in the ministry of revenue, then remonstrance official and censor in chief.
units.literal: The next year Zaili governed Fuyang; Min again observed mourning; when mourning ended he was made director in the Ministry of Revenue, changed to remonstrance official and censor in chief.

units.zh: 時敏父鹹式年七十，鹹式之父年九十餘，供養二尊，朝夕無懈。
units.en: Min's father Xianshi was seventy; Xianshi's father was over ninety; they supported both elders without slackening.
units.literal: At the time Min's father Xianshi was seventy; Xianshi's father was more than ninety; they supported both elders morning and evening without slackening.

units.zh: 鹹式以敏貴，得秘書監致仕。
units.en: Because Min was honored, Xianshi was made secretariat supervisor and retired.
units.literal: Because Min was honored, Xianshi received the Secretariat as supervisor and retired.

units.zh: 敏為兵部侍郎，奉使幽州，鄉里耆舊留宴盡歡。
units.en: As vice minister of war on embassy to You, old friends feasted him endlessly.
units.literal: Min as vice minister of war on embassy to You Prefecture was detained by old friends of the district in feasts of full joy.

units.zh: 馮赟為北京留守，奏敏為副，赟入掌樞密，敏為吏部侍郎。
units.en: Feng Yun, regent of the northern capital, made Min his deputy; when Yun took military affairs, Min was vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: Feng Yun was northern capital regent and memorialized Min as deputy; when Yun entered to hold military affairs, Min was vice minister of personnel.

units.zh: 敏學術不甚長，然外柔而內剛，愛決斷大計。
units.en: Min's scholarship was not deep, but outwardly gentle and inwardly firm, he loved deciding great plans.
units.literal: Min's learning was not very deep, yet outwardly gentle and inwardly firm, he loved to decide great plans.

units.zh: 清泰末，從唐末帝在懷州，時趙德鈞父子有異圖，晉安寨旦夕憂陷，末帝計無從出，問計於從臣。
units.en: At Qingtai's end he was with the Tang final emperor at Huai; the Zhao Dejun father and son plotted; the Jin'an camp feared collapse; the emperor asked his followers for a plan.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai he followed the Tang final emperor at Huai Prefecture; Zhao Dejun and his son had ulterior designs; the Jin'an camp feared falling any day; the final emperor had no plan and asked his followers.

units.zh: 敏奏曰：「臣有一計，請以援兵從東丹王李贊華取幽州路趨西樓，契丹主必有北顧之患。」
units.en: Min said, "I have a plan: take relief troops with the eastern Danyu king Li Zanhua by the Youzhou road to Xilou—the Khitan ruler will have to look north."
units.literal: Min memorialized: "Your servant has one plan: please take relief troops by the eastern Danyu King Li Zanhua along the Youzhou road toward Xilou—the Khitan ruler will surely have the worry of looking north."

units.zh: 末帝然之，而不能用。
units.en: The final emperor agreed but could not adopt it.
units.literal: The final emperor agreed but could not use it.

units.zh: 敏又謂末帝親將李懿曰：「君連姻帝戚，社稷之危，不俟翹足，安得默默茍全耶！」
units.en: Min also told Li Yi, "You are the emperor's kin by marriage; the realm's peril is immediate—how can you seek only your own safety?"
units.literal: Min also told the final emperor's close general Li Yi: "You are allied by marriage to the imperial clan; the state's peril does not await lifting a foot—how can you silently seek only your own safety!"

units.zh: 懿因籌德鈞必破蕃軍之狀，敏曰：「仆燕人也，諳趙德鈞之為人，膽小謀拙，所長者守城寨、嬰壕塹、篤勵健兒耳！
units.en: Yi reckoned Dejun would break the barbarians; Min said, "I am a Yan man and know Dejun—timid in counsel, good only at holding forts, digging ditches, and cheering stout soldiers!
units.literal: Yi then calculated that Dejun would surely break the barbarian army; Min said: "Your servant is a Yan man and knows Zhao Dejun's character—timid in counsel, skilled only at holding forts, manning ditches, and cheering stout soldiers!

units.zh: 若見大敵，奮不顧身，摧堅陷陣，必不能矣。
units.en: Before a great foe he will not throw himself forward, break lines, and charge—he cannot.
units.literal: If he sees a great enemy, he will not throw away his body, break the solid, and charge the ranks—he surely cannot.

units.zh: 況名位震主，奸以謀身乎！
units.en: And when fame and rank overshadow the throne, is he not scheming for himself?
units.literal: Moreover, fame and position that shake the ruler—does he not scheme for himself with treachery!

units.zh: 仆有狂策，不知濟否，茍能必行，亦救寨之一術也。」
units.en: I have a bold plan—I do not know if it will work, but if it can be done, it may yet save the camp."
units.literal: Your servant has a bold plan; I do not know whether it will succeed, but if it can surely be carried out, it is also one method to save the camp."

units.zh: 懿請言之，曰：「如聞駕前馬僅有五千匹，請於其間選壯馬精甲健夫千人，仆願與郎萬金二人
units.en: Yi asked him to explain; he said, "I hear there are only five thousand horses with the imperial train—choose a thousand stout mounts, fine armor, and strong men; I wish to go with Lang Wanjin and you two
units.literal: Yi asked him to speak; he said: "I hear there are only five thousand horses before the imperial carriage—please choose from among them a thousand stout horses, fine armor, and strong men; your servant wishes to go with Lang Wanjin and you two

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：郎萬金為陳州刺史。
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Lang Wanjin was prefect of Chen.
units.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: Lang Wanjin was prefect of Chen.

units.zh: 胡三省云：萬金，當時勇將也。）〉
units.en: Hu Sansheng notes: Wanjin was a renowned warrior of the day.)〉
units.literal: Hu Sansheng says: Wanjin was a valiant general of the time.)〉

units.zh: 路出山，夜冒敵騎，循山入大寨，千騎之內，得其半濟，則寨無虞矣。
units.en: By a mountain path, strike the enemy cavalry by night, follow the mountain into the great camp, and catch half their thousand riders mid-crossing—the camp will be safe.
units.literal: by a mountain road, by night strike the enemy cavalry, follow the mountain into the great camp, and within the thousand riders take half while they are crossing—then the camp will be secure.

units.zh: 張敬達等幽閉，不知朝廷援兵近遠，若知大軍在團柏谷中，雖鐵障亦可沖踏，況敵騎乎！」
units.en: Zhang Jingda and the rest are trapped and do not know whether relief is near; if they knew the main army was in Tuanbai Valley, even iron barriers could be broken—how much more enemy cavalry!"
units.literal: Zhang Jingda and the others are shut in and do not know how near or far the court's relief army is; if they knew the great army was in Tuanbai Valley, even an iron barrier could be charged down—how much more so enemy cavalry!"

units.zh: 末帝聞之曰：「龍敏之心極壯，用之晚矣。」
units.en: The final emperor said, "Long Min's heart is exceedingly bold—we employed him too late."
units.literal: The final emperor heard this and said: "Long Min's heart is exceedingly bold—he was employed too late."

units.zh: 人亦以為大言，然其慷慨感激，皆此類也。
units.en: Others called it bravado, yet his generous passion was always of this kind.
units.literal: People also regarded it as grand talk, yet his generous indignation was all of this kind.

units.zh: 晉祖受命，敏以本官判戶部，遷尚書左丞。
units.en: When the Jin founder took power, Min retained his post while overseeing revenue and was promoted to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When the Jin founder received the Mandate, Min in his existing office oversaw the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，復本官，俄移太常卿。
units.en: After his father's death he mourned; when mourning ended he resumed his former post and was soon made Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when mourning ended he resumed his original office, and soon was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 開運中，奉命使越。
units.en: In Kaiyun he was sent on embassy to Yue.
units.literal: During Kaiyun he was ordered on embassy to Yue.

units.zh: 先是，朝臣將命，必拜起於浙帥，敏至，抗揖而已，識者多之。
units.en: Previously court envoys would bow before the Zhe commander; Min arrived and returned only a formal bow with folded arms, and the discerning praised him.
units.literal: Previously, when court ministers received imperial commissions they invariably bowed and rose before the Zhe commander; when Min arrived he returned only a formal bow with folded arms, and the discerning praised him.

units.zh: 使還，改工部尚書。
units.en: On his return he was made minister of works.
units.literal: On returning from his mission he was made minister of works.

units.zh: 乾祐元年春，疽發於背，聞高祖晏駕，乃扶病於私第，縞素而臨，後旬日卒於家，時年六十三。
units.en: In the spring of Qianyou year one a carbuncle broke out on his back. Learning that Gaozu had died, he dragged himself from his home in mourning dress to attend, and ten days later died at home at sixty-three.
units.literal: In the spring of the first year of Qianyou a boil erupted on his back; hearing that Gaozu had died, he supported his illness at his private residence and went in white mourning to attend; ten days later he died at home, aged sixty-three.

units.zh: 隱帝嗣位，詔贈右僕射。
units.en: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, an edict posthumously made him right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, an edict posthumously granted him right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 劉鼎，字公度，徐州蕭縣人。
units.en: Liu Ding, styled Gongdu, was from Xiao County in Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Liu Ding, styled Gongdu, was a native of Xiao County in Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 祖泰，蕭縣令。
units.en: His grandfather Tai was magistrate of Xiao County.
units.literal: His grandfather Tai was magistrate of Xiao County.

units.zh: 父崇，梁太祖微時，常傭力崇家，及即位，召崇用之，歷殿中監、商州刺史。
units.en: His father Chong had employed the future Liang Taizu as a laborer when the latter was obscure; when Taizu took the throne he recalled Chong and promoted him through director of the palace bureau and prefect of Shang.
units.literal: His father Chong, when the Liang Taizu was still obscure, often hired out his labor to Chong's house; when Taizu took the throne he summoned Chong and employed him, and Chong served as director of the palace bureau and prefect of Shang Prefecture.

units.zh: 崇之母撫梁祖有恩，梁氏號為「國婆」，徐、宋之民謂崇家為「豢龍劉家」。
units.en: Chong's mother had nursed the Liang founder and was called "State Grandmother" by the Liang house; people in Xu and Song called the family the "Dragon-Raising Liu."
units.literal: Chong's mother had shown kindness in raising the Liang founder, and the Liang house called her "State Grandmother"; the people of Xu and Song called Chong's family the "Dragon-Raising Liu Family."

units.zh: 鼎起家為大理評事，歷尚書博士、殿中侍郎史、起居郎。
units.en: Ding began as a judging official in the Court of Judicial Review, then served as secretariat erudite, palace censor, and recorder of the ruler's movements.
units.literal: Ding began his career as a judging official of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as erudite of the Secretariat, palace censor, and recorder of the ruler's movements.

units.zh: 清泰中，自吏部員外郎出為渾州廉判，入為刑部郎中，充鹽鐵判官，改吏部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: In Qingtai he went out from vice director of personnel to serve as integrity assessor of Hun Prefecture, then returned as director in the ministry of punishments, salt-and-iron judging official, and finally director of personnel with concurrent attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business.
units.literal: In Qingtai he left the post of vice director in the Ministry of Personnel to become integrity assessor of Hun Prefecture, entered court as director in the Ministry of Punishments, served as salt and iron judging official, and was changed to director in the Ministry of Personnel concurrently with attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.

units.zh: 乾祐初，拜諫議大夫，卒年五十五。
units.en: Early in Qianyou he was made remonstrance official and died at fifty-five.
units.literal: Early in Qianyou he was appointed remonstrance official and died at fifty-five.

units.zh: 鼎善交遊，能談笑。
units.en: Ding made friends easily and was gifted at witty conversation.
units.literal: Ding was skilled at friendship and could banter with ease.

units.zh: 居家仁孝，事繼母趙氏甚謹，異母昆仲凡七人，撫之如一。
units.en: At home he was filial; he served his stepmother Lady Zhao devotedly and treated seven half-brothers as one.
units.literal: At home he was filial and kind; he served his stepmother Lady Zhao with great care; among seven half-brothers he treated them all alike.

units.zh: 性若寬易，而典選曹按吏有風棱，人稱為能。
units.en: He seemed easygoing by nature, yet in the personnel bureau his handling of officials was sharp-edged, and he was reckoned capable.
units.literal: His nature seemed easygoing, yet in managing the personnel bureau and investigating officials he had stern authority, and people called him capable.

units.zh: 子袞，登進士第，文彩遒雋。
units.en: His son Gun passed the jinshi; his prose was forceful and elegant.
units.literal: His son Gun passed the jinshi examination; his writing was forceful and elegant.

units.zh: 仕周為左拾遺、直史館，早卒。
units.en: In Zhou he was left remonstrance official and direct historiographer and died young.
units.literal: He served Zhou as left remonstrance official and direct historiographer and died young.

units.zh: 張允，鎮州束鹿人。
units.en: Zhang Yun was from Shulu in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhang Yun was a native of Shulu in Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 父徵。
units.en: His father was Zheng.
units.literal: His father was Zheng.

units.zh: 允幼學為儒，仕本州為參軍。
units.en: Yun studied Confucian learning in youth and served his prefecture as military adjutant.
units.literal: Yun in youth studied as a Confucian and served his prefecture as military adjutant.

units.zh: 張文禮之據州叛，莊宗致討，允隨文禮子處瑾請降於鄴，不許，與處瑾並系於獄。
units.en: When Zhang Wenli rebelled and held the prefecture, Zhuangzong attacked; Yun followed Wenli's son Chujin to sue for surrender at Ye, was refused, and was imprisoned with Chujin.
units.literal: When Zhang Wenli seized the prefecture in rebellion, Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against him; Yun followed Wenli's son Chujin to request surrender at Ye but was not permitted and was imprisoned with Chujin.

units.zh: 鎮、冀平，宥之，留於鄴，署本府功曹。
units.en: When Zhen and Ji were pacified he was spared, stayed at Ye, and was made merit officer of the prefectural office.
units.literal: When Zhen and Ji were pacified he was pardoned, remained at Ye, and was appointed merit officer of the prefectural office.

units.zh: 趙在禮嬰城叛，署節度推官，從歷滄、兗二鎮書記，入為監察御史，歷右補闕、起居舍人，充宏文館直學士、水部員外郎、知制誥。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili rebelled and held the city he was military investigating officer; he served as secretary at Cang and Yan, entered as investigating censor, rose through right censor and recorder, was Hongwen Hall academician, vice director of water, and drafted edicts.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili held the city in rebellion he was appointed investigating officer of the military commission; he followed through as secretary at Cang and Yan, entered court as investigating censor, served as right censor and recorder, was direct academician of the Hongwen Hall, vice director of water, and drafted edicts.

units.zh: 清泰初，皇子重美為河南尹，典六軍諸衛事，時朝廷選參佐，以允剛介，改給事中，充六軍判官。
units.en: Early in Qingtai Prince Chongmei governed Henan and the Six Armies guards; Yun's stern integrity won him appointment as attendant and Six Armies judge.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai Prince Chongmei was Henan governor in charge of the Six Armies guards; the court selected aides; because Yun was stern and upright he was changed to attendant and made judge of the Six Armies.

units.zh: 尋罷職，轉左散騎常侍。
units.en: Soon he left that post and became left regular cavalry attendant.
units.literal: Soon his post was removed and he was transferred to left regular cavalry attendant.

units.zh: 晉天福初，允以國朝頻有肆赦，乃進「駁赦論」，曰：「《管子》云：『凡赦者小利而大害，久而不勝其禍；
units.en: Early in Jin's Tianfu era, with frequent general amnesties, Yun submitted a "Refutation of Amnesty," citing the Guanzi: "Amnesty brings small profit and great harm—in time the harm prevails;
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu, because the dynasty frequently issued general amnesties, Yun submitted a "Refutation of Amnesty," saying: "The Guanzi says: 'Amnesties are small profit and great harm—in time one cannot overcome the disaster;

units.zh: 無赦者小害而大利，久而不勝其福。』
units.en: no amnesty is small harm and great profit—in time the blessing prevails.
units.literal: no amnesty is small harm and great profit—in time one cannot overcome the blessing.

units.zh: 又《漢紀》云：『吳漢疾篤，帝問所欲言。
units.en: The Han Annals also say: Wu Han lay gravely ill; the emperor asked what he wished to say.
units.literal: Also the Han Annals say: 'Wu Han was gravely ill; the emperor asked what he wished to say.

units.zh: 對曰：唯願陛下無為赦耳。』
units.en: He replied: I only wish Your Majesty never to grant amnesty.
units.literal: He replied: I only wish Your Majesty never to grant amnesty.

units.zh: 如是者何？
units.en: Why is this?
units.literal: Why is this?

units.zh: 蓋行赦不以為恩，不行赦亦不以為無恩，為罰有罪故也。
units.en: Amnesty is not grace, and withholding it is not cruelty—punishment belongs to the guilty.
units.literal: Because granting amnesty is not taken as grace, and not granting amnesty is not taken as lack of grace—it is because punishment is for the guilty.

units.zh: 竊觀自古帝王，皆以水旱則降德音而宥過，開狴牢以放囚，冀感天心以救其災者，非也。
units.en: Since antiquity emperors facing flood or drought have issued virtuous edicts, pardoned crimes, and opened prisons to move Heaven—this is wrong.
units.literal: I observe that from antiquity emperors, when there were floods or drought, would issue edicts of virtue and pardon offenses, open the prisons and release prisoners, hoping to move Heaven's heart to save the disaster—this is wrong.

units.zh: 假有二人訟，一有罪，一無罪，若有罪者見舍，則無罪者銜冤，銜冤者彼何疏，見舍者此何親乎？
units.en: If two litigants stand, one guilty and one innocent, pardoning the guilty leaves the innocent aggrieved—why favor the guilty and wrong the innocent?
units.literal: Suppose two men sue, one guilty and one innocent; if the guilty is pardoned, the innocent harbors grievance—why is the aggrieved party neglected and the pardoned party favored?

units.zh: 如此則是致災之道，非救災之術也。
units.en: That is the way to invite disaster, not to end it.
units.literal: Such is the way to bring disaster, not the art of saving it.

units.zh: 自此小民遇天災則喜，皆相勸為惡，曰國家好行赦，必赦我以救災，如此即是國家教民為惡也。
units.en: Then commoners facing disaster rejoice and urge one another to crime, saying the state loves amnesty and will pardon them to end the calamity—the state thus teaches evil.
units.literal: From then on common people meeting natural disaster rejoice and urge one another to do evil, saying the state loves amnesty and will surely pardon them to save the disaster—thus the state teaches the people to do evil.

units.zh: 且天道福善禍淫，若以舍為惡之人，而便變災為福，則又是天助其惡民也。
units.en: Heaven blesses the good and punishes the wicked; to pardon the wicked and turn disaster to blessing is to make Heaven aid the wicked.
units.literal: Moreover Heaven's way blesses the good and punishes the wicked; if by pardoning the wicked one turns disaster to blessing, then Heaven is helping wicked people.

units.zh: 細而論之，必不然矣。
units.en: Examined closely, it cannot be so.
units.literal: Examined in detail, it surely cannot be so.

units.zh: 儻或天降之災，蓋欲警誡人主。
units.en: Perhaps Heaven sends disaster to warn the ruler.
units.literal: Perhaps when Heaven sends disaster it is to warn and admonish the ruler.

units.zh: 節嗜欲，務勤儉，恤鰥寡，正刑罰，不濫舍有罪，不僭殺無辜，使美化行於下，聖德聞於上，則雖有水旱，亦不為沴矣。
units.en: Restrain desire, practice thrift, pity widows and orphans, correct punishments, do not rashly pardon the guilty or kill the innocent—let virtue spread below and sagely fame above—then flood and drought will not harm.
